source_review.notes: Checked thirteen primary sources: the MillWheel paper; current Apache Flink state, snapshot, schema, TTL-migration, and large-state documentation; current Apache Beam state/timer and runner contracts; current Kafka Streams state-store/restoration documentation; and current Spark arbitrary-state/configuration documentation. All cited URLs returned HTTP 200. Product behavior and version-qualified migration support are explicitly attributed.

evidence: Reviewed per-key state s_k,i, input e_i, versioned transition T_v, outputs O_i, timer delta Theta_i, live keys K, and content/overhead bytes b_k,j/h_k,j.
Checked key, namespace, operator/state UID, serializer/schema, timer identity, key group, checkpoint cut, and external-effect identity remain distinct.
Checked decimal GB/KB, seconds/hours, key/entry/group counts, TTL strictness, and checkpoint half-open input ranges use explicit units/conventions.
notation_and_syntax.notes: State-machine notation is scoped to declared per-key ordering; representation equality is distinguished from semantic equivalence.

evidence: Executed stateful-transition-ttl with Python 3.14.4 and reproduced four accepted events, one duplicate, evictions (a,b), final state {'a':(1,9)}, and four retained dedup IDs.
Recomputed examples: 20M*(40+56)=1.92 GB; 100*(24+40)=6.4 KB per key and about 6.4 GB per million keys; key-group averages 32 then 16.
Recomputed exercises: 12M*(24+40+2*48)=1.92 GB and 3.168 GB at 65% amplification; TTL 38*1.2=45.6 hours; 4096/64=64 and 4096/160=25.6 groups per instance.
Checked checkpoint mismatch example: pairing state through 849 with source 800 duplicates 50 transitions, while old state with source 850 skips them.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Arithmetic verifies declared base estimates and one local state transition; no backend, checkpoint, restore, or distributed performance benchmark is claimed.

evidence: Checked T_v(s,e)=(s',O,Theta) includes initialization, duplicate, order, error, timer, output, and deletion semantics needed for deterministic replay.
Verified working storage sum over live key/state entries of b+h has byte dimensions while caches, logs, compaction, snapshots, and headroom are named additional terms.
Checked consistent recovery requires source positions and every state/timer image from one admitted prefix; mismatched cuts cause skips or duplicate transitions.
Verified TTL boundary now-last_write>duration keeps equality and expires only beyond, and rescaling assigns each stable key group exactly once.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Determinism is semantic under pinned ordering/version and declared numerical tolerance; it does not require byte-identical backend representations.

evidence: Reviewed empty/missing/null state, first update, duplicate/reordered/late input, poison records, transition errors, deletions, timer replacement, overdue timers, and TTL at/before/after boundary.
Reviewed zero/millions of keys, giant nested values, hot keys, unbounded maps/lists/timers, state skew, counter overflow, nondeterministic iteration, and physical write amplification.

Reviewed crash during update/checkpoint/restore/rescale/migration, partial/corrupt snapshot/changelog, stale standby, key-group omission/duplication, source-position mismatch, and ambiguous external effects.
Reviewed serializer/key changes, operator/state rename, TTL enable/disable, broadcast reordering, disk/memory exhaustion, credential expiry, residency, deletion, backup, and legal hold.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Transition correctness, recovery cut, physical capacity, schema migration, timer/TTL lifecycle, external effects, and privacy can fail independently.

evidence: Traced one qualified input through key routing, managed-state read/transition/write, timer/output delta, consistent checkpoint, failure restore, replay, and external-effect protection.
Checked one current owner per keyed shard and exactly-one eligible owner per key group across rescaling, including restored timers/state before effects.
Checked operator UID, state name, key/namespace, serializer/schema, code/time/TTL versions, source positions, and snapshot integrity remain compatible.
Checked bounds cover keys/entries/value tails, timers, buffers, heap/native/disk, WAL/compaction, snapshots, changelogs, standbys, restore, migration, and cleanup.
invariant_checking.notes: Working backend, durable checkpoint, changelog, standby, cache, and external source of truth have separate roles and failure assumptions.

evidence: Reviewed the ten-step audit from durable transition identity through scoped ownership, backend economics, bounds, consistent cut, effect protocol, TTL, rescaling, migration, and lifecycle.
Checked replay determinism requires same qualified input order, compatible initial state, code/schema version, and captured nondeterministic inputs.
Checked consistent-cut proof covers managed state/timers and emitted data, while external effects are excluded absent transaction/idempotency/outbox/fencing.

Reviewed counterexamples for local-disk durability, checkpoint-as-backend, exactly-once API calls, TTL-as-memory-only, expired-as-erased, timers-as-exact, schema/key compatibility, and total-bytes health.
proof_review.notes: General state principles are separated from Flink, Beam, Kafka Streams, Spark, and MillWheel-specific mechanisms.

evidence: Audited uses of deterministic, durable, local, checkpointed, exactly-once, idempotent, authoritative, compatible, expired, deleted, rescalable, and atomic.
Confirmed strong claims name their scope: state versus effects, current owner, compatible snapshot, key/namespace, time domain, serializer version, and supported engine behavior.
Confirmed current/version-qualified engine features are sourced, and the executable example disclaims distributed/checkpoint/backend semantics.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No backend, checkpoint, TTL, timer, changelog, or migration feature is mislabeled as universal end-to-end correctness or secure deletion.

evidence: Reviewed measures for keys/entries/bytes/value tails, access latency, cache/backend memory/disk, WAL/compaction, timers, TTL cleanup, checkpoint, restore, and rescale movement.
Reviewed correlations with input/backpressure/lag, hot keys, GC/native memory, disk, snapshot limits, changelog lag, sink latency, and cleanup debt.
Confirmed no universal backend, state type, TTL, key-group count, checkpoint interval, changelog/standby policy, compaction setting, or migration strategy is prescribed.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Production selection requires representative access/update distributions, state/value tails, failure and restore objectives, engine/backend versions, topology, security, and policy.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed stateful operators as versioned state machines with keyed/operator/broadcast scopes, typed access, distinct working/durable stores, physical economics, consistent recovery, timers, TTL, bounds, skew, rescaling, migration, control state, effects, observability, and lifecycle.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed practical minimal-state design, backend selection, physical sizing, checkpoint coupling, timer/TTL contracts, hot-key mitigation, key-group restore, production-byte migration rehearsal, transactional/idempotent effects, protected diagnostics, fault injection, rollback, and deletion. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from transition/state scope through storage/recovery and lifecycle operations. Ten examples and five answered exercises cover minimal state, overhead, checkpoint cuts, dedup TTL, expiry boundaries, timers, key groups, schema semantics, deterministic transitions, capacity, restore, rescaling, and upgrade review.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external Flink, Beam, Kafka Streams, or Spark maintainer, stream-processing/state-backend/database researcher, storage/runtime/performance/SRE engineer, schema-migration or security/privacy specialist, records/legal authority, affected-tenant reviewer, accessibility specialist, or certification review is claimed.
